title: Pilot: canary rollforward readiness & nested routing check
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on readiness for canary rollforward, routing priorities for nested VPC paths, and one-off kernel upgrade plan. Discussed fallbacks, KMS audit requirement and timing for cutover. Agreed to a short soak with controlled traffic profile and three clear rollback triggers.
action_items: Alex Monroe: Share final rollforward playbook + runbook links (due 2027-10-01)
Priya Singh: Run the 2-hour high-qps soak and upload telemetry snapshot (due 2027-09-30)
Jordan Price: Validate egress ACL for staged canary ranges and confirm with cloud team (due 2027-09-29)
Samira Khan: Provide KMS key rotation window constraints and SOC2 reporting requirements (due 2027-10-02)
Diego: Stage kernel upgrade on one node group and report latencies (due 2027-09-30)
next_steps: Redwood to enable circuit-breaker threshold at 2.5x baseline tail latency
Customer to run synthetic traffic with 60/40 prefix locality mix and send results
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-09-28 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Recording: Auto
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Jordan Price (Halcyon NetOps), Taylor Reed (Halcyon CTO), Samira Khan (Halcyon Security), Diego (Halcyon SRE), Rita (App Owner)

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda - canary rollforward readiness, nested routing check, kernel/quant upgrade status, and security gating. We'll try to keep it tight.
[00:18] Jordan: Yeah, thanks Alex, quick heads up, we're a little behind on the cloud egress ACLs but planning to finish tomorrow, so want to make sure that doesn't block the canary.
[00:30] Priya (SE): Okay noted, if the ACLs miss the window we can still run a private canary within the VPC, but latency profile will be a bit different because of the nat egress.
[00:45] Taylor (CTO): The big ask from our side is a clean rollback path and clear triggers. Last week the fallback didn't flip as expected when we hit the 99.9 tail.
[01:05] Alex: Totally. We've updated the runbook to include three explicit triggers - sustained 2x baseline p95 for five minutes, error-rate >1% for two minutes, or KV cache miss storm leading to memory pressure. If any trigger fires the orchestrator will route traffic to the warm fallback pool.
[01:30] Rita (App Owner): Sorry quick interjection, when you say KV cache miss storm, do you mean the prefix cache, or the per-session KV? We saw a big dip when our test set had new prefixes.
[01:45] Priya: Good question, Rita. It's primarily prefix cache (we sometimes transcribe as KV cash in notes sorry), so the prefix/KV cache priming is important. Our suggested plan includes a priming step in the first 10% traffic window.
[02:10] Jordan: On routing - we need to confirm nested route preference. Our netops team wants traffic to stick local to the nearest AZ when possible, but to force fallback to a different region if latency crosses threshold. Is that policy expressible in the Redwood routing policy?
[02:30] Priya: Yes, you can express multi-tier policy: prefer AZ-local -> if tail latency > X ms or loss > Y% then prefer region fallback -> if capacity exhausted then go to hosted fallback. The policy can be encoded and we can provide a policy bundle for you.
[02:55] Diego (SRE): When you say region fallback, are you talking about switching model variant or just routing to another identical pool? We have concerns about model parity and quant quirks affecting output.
[03:15] Alex: For this pilot we're going to keep model variant stable; fallback is identical model on different capacity. We will not change quant or compilation profile during canary to avoid confounding quality. Kernel upgrades are separate and only in the canary node group.
[03:40] Taylor: Okay that reduces risk. On the kernel/quant upgrade, Diego ran a small stencil yesterday and saw 8-12% tail increases on long context (3k tokens) on one node after the newer kernel. Is that expected?
[04:00] Priya: We did see some outlying tail with the early kernel+opt paths, expected in early NPU scheduling. The mitigation is to pin kernel selection for long-context requests or to throttle batching for those sequences. For the rollforward we're proposing to stage kernel on 10% nodes and only route short-sequence traffic.
[04:25] Jordan: Sounds reasonable. If we stage on 10% nodes, what metrics do you want us to watch? We need the specific dashboards so our SREs can automate watch rules.
[04:40] Priya: Monitor p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU steal, GPU occupancy, KV cache miss rate, and cputime per token. We'll send a dashboard link. Also, enable the trace hook; it helps assign requests to path variants.
[05:05] Samira (Security): Looping security in — KMS keys, audit logs. We need to confirm key rotation windows and that Redwood's private control plane will emit S3-compatible audit trails to our SIEM.
[05:25] Alex: Short answer: yes. For the private deployment we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and we stream audit events to your forwarders. There is a short list of events (model loads, key ops, route changes) that are emitted. We'll share the exact mapping.
[05:45] Samira: Also we need a SOC2 attestation copy and a list of sub-processors for compliance.
[05:55] Alex: We'll attach the SOC2 redacted pack in follow-up.
[06:05] Rita: Back to the canary timeline - what are we targeting for the roll? Tomorrow? Wednesday?
[06:15] Jordan: Our cloud team can confirm egress ACLs by EOD tomorrow, so Tuesday night soak is possible if Redwood is ready.
[06:30] Priya: We can do a controlled 2-hour soak Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC with a 60/40 locality traffic mix and synthetic loads matching production P95 token lengths. We'll tag the traffic so we can debug.
[06:50] Alex: Great. During the soak we'll have two automatic guardrails: circuit-breaker at 2.5x baseline tail latency and error-rate guard at 1%. Both flip to fallback and auto-notify the SRE channel.
[07:10] Diego: Who owns the manual abort? If the automations flip but we want to keep it to investigate, can we hold?
[07:25] Priya: Yes, automated fallback will run but it notifies human channels. There's a single manual abort owner on your side - we can set that to Jordan. If you hit abort, the orchestrator respects hold for up to 30 minutes for postmortem.
[07:45] Taylor: On telemetry retention, how long will Redwood keep the per-request traces for analysis? We may need 90 days for compliance.
[08:00] Alex: By default private pilot retains 30 days; enterprise add-on can extend to 90 days. We can toggle retention for the pilot if you need more, but there might be storage charges.
[08:15] Samira: We'll want 90 days for the canary window at least. Please include cost estimate.
[08:25] Alex: Noted.
[08:30] Jordan: One more tricky thing — nested routing: a subset of our users are behind corporate proxies that proxy through an internal gateway which changes source IPs. This broke our previous prefix locality heuristics.
[08:50] Priya: We do have headers-based affinity. If you can tag the user request with the X-Forwarded-User or a custom header, we can use that to preserve affinity. If not, we'll fall back to deterministic hashing and a session cookie.
[09:10] Rita: We can't change client headers for the moment. We'll need deterministic hashing. What is the risk of hot-shard with hashing?
[09:25] Priya: Hot-shard risk exists if your user distribution is skewed. We recommend prefix priming and some jittered hashing to smooth hot keys. The runbook includes a priming traffic generator.
[09:40] Diego: Ok Diego: (mumbles) we'll set that up.
[09:50] Alex: Quick recap and explicit next steps. Priya will run the soak and upload telemetry by Thu, Diego to stage kernel on one node, Jordan to confirm ACLs tomorrow EOD, Samira to send KMS window. We'll share the canary runbook and the dashboard.
[10:10] Taylor: Fine, as long as we have a clear rollback and the 3 triggers are in place.
[10:25] Alex: Yes, final rollforward playbook will include the triggers and manual abort ownership. We'll send the doc and schedule the soak. Anything else?
[10:35] Samira: One last ask — please add the SIEM event mapping and the minimal PII redaction flows for our compliance team.
[10:45] Alex: Will do. Thanks all, we'll follow up with links and the scheduled calendar invite for the soak.
[10:55] End of recording.

Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hearings ("KV cash" vs KV cache), names occasionally shortened. Several references to prior test run notes and dashboards will be provided in follow-up links.
